semantic_correction.stem: Before beginning client teaching, which assessment best addresses readiness to learn?

options.A: Ask how the client prefers to learn and whether the client feels ready and interested in discussing the information at this time.
options.B: Begin with the standard teaching materials and adjust the method later if the client appears confused or loses interest during the session.
options.C: Choose the teaching method based on the nurse's usual approach, then assess learning preferences after the main content has been presented.
options.D: Schedule the teaching near discharge so the information is recent, even when the client is willing and able to learn earlier in the stay.

semantic_correction.rationale: A is correct. The current Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 12, specifically recommends assessing patients' learning style and readiness to learn. AHRQ advises asking how the patient prefers to learn and matching education materials to that preference. It also recommends confirming that the patient is ready and interested in learning, noting that some patients may not be ready for extensive information immediately after a new diagnosis. Therefore the nurse should assess both preferred learning approach and readiness before or as teaching begins. B and C are incorrect because they postpone the assessment until after teaching has already started. D is incorrect because education should be timed to readiness and need rather than delayed to a fixed discharge point when the client is ready earlier.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Assess the client's preferred learning approach and readiness or interest before providing health education so teaching can be adapted to the client's needs.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: removed the absolute-word and answer-length cues, rebuilt all four teaching-assessment approaches to comparable length and specificity, freshly verified current AHRQ Tool 12 guidance, and preserved assessment of learning preference plus readiness as the single best response.

audit_findings_append.finding: The revised item tests readiness-to-learn assessment with one clearly best response, balanced alternatives, current AHRQ guidance, and no absolute-word or length cue.

option_audit.A: Correct. It directly matches AHRQ's recommendation to assess both learning preference and readiness to learn.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. Teaching begins before readiness and learning preference are assessed, reducing the ability to tailor education effectively.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. The nurse's usual method should not replace assessment of the client's preferred learning approach before presenting the main content.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. Education should be timed to the client's readiness and clinical needs rather than delayed to a fixed discharge point.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A uniquely assesses both learning preference and readiness before teaching; B-C assess too late and D uses an arbitrary timing rule.
cueing_check: All four options are parallel teaching-planning approaches of comparable length and specificity; the prior 'all' distractor and uniquely-long correct response were removed.
